# Girafe Ingestor Plugin

> **This plugin project is incomplete.** Implement `read_dataset()` before this plugin can produce output. Until then, ingestion runs raise `NotImplementedError` the first time it is called. Set `TIME_DIM` at the top of the ingestor too: ingestion stops with `NotImplementedError` until it names the time dimension your reader returns.

## Development

This project has its own Python environment. Run every `firecube` command in
this README from this directory through `uv run`, so the plugin, Firecube, and
the CLI all resolve from the same environment. To install the plugin into an
existing Firecube environment instead, activate that environment and run
`firecube plugins install --editable .` without `uv run`.

```bash
uv sync
```

Implement `read_dataset()` in the generated ingestor, then add behavior-based
tests for the source data and output contract.

```bash
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check .
uv run pyright
```

## Install into Firecube

```bash
uv run firecube plugins install --editable .
uv run firecube plugins list
uv run firecube plugins describe girafe
uv run firecube ingest girafe --show-options
```

`firecube plugins describe` should list `[ENGINE]` options. If you add plugin-specific options via a `PluginConfig` subclass, they will appear under `[PLUGIN]`.

## Run a local ingestion

After the implementation and tests pass, run:

```bash
uv run firecube ingest girafe \
  --input-data /path/to/your/input \
  --target file:///tmp/girafe_out.zarr \
  --product-name girafe \
  --output-format zarr \
  --write-mode direct
```

- `--input-data` takes a directory or a single file. Discovery picks up `.zip`,
  `.h5`, `.nc`, `.nc4`, `.hdf`, and `.he5` files, and HDF5 files without those
  extensions. For other formats, add a filter such as
  `--input-filters '["*.csv"]'`.
- `--product-name` labels the product. It defaults to `PRODUCT_NAME` in the
  ingestor.
- `--write-mode direct` writes into the target as the run goes. `staged` builds
  the output in a local workspace and publishes it at the end.

The data is in the store's `default` group:

```python
import xarray as xr

print(xr.open_zarr("/tmp/girafe_out.zarr", group="default", consolidated=False))
```

## Run again

A second run into the same store is refused. Add
`--option resume_existing=true` to skip timestamps already written and append new
ones, or `--option force_reingest=true` to rewrite them.

## Other targets

For an `s3://bucket/key.zarr` target, use `--write-mode staged`: the run
builds the store in a local workspace and uploads it at the end. Chunking,
compression, and sharding defaults live in `ZarrStorageConfig` in the ingestor.
